summary: Unexpected model-pin eviction after regional edge reshuffle causing cascading fallbacks
description:
Issue summary:
Customer AtlasHealth reports that during a scheduled regional edge reshuffle (us-west), a subset of long-running sessions lost their model version pin and were routed to a fallback variant with degraded generation quality. The event coincided with a canary weight adjustment and an autoscaler preempt/rebalance in the region.

Impact:
- ~12 session streams (of a ~3k tenant cohort) observed abrupt model switch from gptx-8k-v1 (pinned) to gptx-16k-quant fallback.
- Customer saw quality regressions and 5 user-facing incidents (incorrect diagnoses in an internal triage flow).
- No billing disparity reported, but SLA risk for enterprise customer during scheduled maintenance window.

Environment:
- prod cluster: us-west primary, failover us-east
- Tenant: AtlasHealth (enterprise), requests use pinned_model header + session affinity cookie
- Canary rollout in same window: weight shift from 0% -> 10% for new variant of gptx-8k-v1

Observed behavior:
- Edge reshuffle triggered short-lived reinitialization of some sidecar connections.
- Affected sessions show token refresh and Set-Cookie mutation in edge logs immediately prior to pin loss.
- Orchestrator snapshots show that pin metadata remained in control-plane for tenant; however several front-line proxy nodes served traffic without pin-preserving cookie.

Expected behavior:
- Model pin should be preserved for session lifetime across edge node reshuffles and autoscaler rebalance events.
- Fallback routing should only occur when pin is explicitly unbound or when model variant is unavailable, with clear audit trail.

Steps to reproduce (attempted):
1) Start a long-running pinned session for tenant with pinned_model=gptx-8k-v1 and affinity cookie.
2) Initiate a regional edge reshuffle (simulate node drain) while canary weight shift starts.
3) Observe session cookies, Set-Cookie headers, and routing decisions on ingress nodes.
4) Replay identical requests through affected edge node to see if pin is honored.

Logs / Artifacts:
- Edge logs (us-west) attached in artifact: edge-reshuffle-uswest-2026-03-10.tar.gz (traces/headers for affected session IDs).
- Orchestrator snapshot: orchestrator-snap-2026-03-10-23:12
- Session-store traces showing affinity lease renewals for impacted session IDs.
investigation_notes:
Timeline summary:
- 2026-03-10 22:58 UTC: Canary weight adjustment started for cohort that overlaps AtlasHealth tenant.
- 2026-03-10 22:59 UTC: Autoscaler in us-west preempted two low-priority nodes (spot reclaim), triggering an edge reshuffle.
- 2026-03-10 23:00 UTC: Multiple sidecar reconnects seen; Set-Cookie header mutated in 7 of 12 affected session streams.

Hypotheses evaluated:
- Hypothesis A: Orchestrator unbound pins during snapshot merge. Rejected: control-plane shows pin metadata unchanged.
- Hypothesis B: Edge-proxy header sanitizer mutated or dropped the pin cookie during reconnect. Supported by logs showing sidecar rewrite of cookie domain and cookie attributes (HttpOnly -> missing).
- Hypothesis C: Health probe grace period mismatch allowed edge to declare variant unhealthy and trigger fallback routing for live sessions. Partially supported: healthcheck spike correlates with 429/5xx on a small subset of model backends.

Partial findings:
- The cookie mutation occurred only on nodes running edge-proxy v2.4.1 with new cookie normalization codepath. Older nodes preserved cookies.
- A small race between session-lease renewal and sidecar reattach meant the session-store marked the session as 'orphaned' momentarily, enabling fallback logic.
- Canary weight shift increased routing churn and made race window more likely.

Immediate mitigation applied (2026-03-11 00:30 UTC):
- Rolled back edge-proxy normalization flag on impacted nodes to preserve cookie attributes.
- Increased session-lease grace to 6s from 2s for affected fleet as emergency measure.

Next steps planned:
- Engineering to revert the cookie normalization changes or add explicit pin-preserve exceptions in edge-proxy. PR to follow.
- Adjust canary rollouts to avoid overlapping with regional rebalances for enterprise tenants by adding blackout window.
- Add stronger invariants: edge must consult control-plane pin store before allowing fallback for pinned sessions.
resolution: In progress: temporary mitigations (edge-proxy flag rollback + session-lease grace increase) restored pin stability for AtlasHealth sessions; full fix requires an edge-proxy code patch to preserve pin cookies during reconnect and a scheduler change to avoid canary-rebalance overlap. Engineering draft PR created and scheduled for staged rollout. Post-incident follow-up: propose new canary blackout window policy for enterprise tenants and update runbook to include cookie-preserve check.
comments: Maya Chen (Support) - 2026-03-10: Customer reported sudden model swaps during our scheduled window; provided session IDs and sample outputs. Logged as P1 given enterprise SLA.
Raj Patel (SRE) - 2026-03-10: Initial triage points to edge cookie mutation during sidecar reconnect. Pulling edge logs and orchestrator snapshots.
Anika Verma (Eng - Edge) - 2026-03-11: Reproduced cookie rewrite on edge-proxy v2.4.1 when running cookie-normalization enabled. Preparing rollback and patch to skip normalization for "pin" cookies.
Raj Patel (SRE) - 2026-03-11: Emergency rollback of normalization flag complete for us-west, observing pins stable in monitored cohort (10/10 sessions remain pinned after rollback).
Customer (AtlasHealth - Support Contact: Jorge Alvarez) - 2026-03-11: Confirmed that previously affected workflows are now returning to expected models; requested root cause and prevention steps.

Anika Verma (Eng - Edge) - 2026-03-12: Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1123 adds explicit pin cookie whitelist and strengthens cookie attr preservation during reconnects. Scheduling staged rollout to canary subset next week.

Priya Das (Product) - 2026-03-12: Recommend we add enterprise blackout policy to canary scheduler and update customer-facing maintenance page to list blackout windows. Filing follow-up ticket to product backlog.
